open_points.subject: Authorization of access-management records
open_points.text: “Project-scoped access requires session ... + project grant/assignment” conflicts with R0-16, which makes grants and assignments project-scoped, and the common rule, which lets an administrator create or revoke them without an existing project grant or assignment.
open_points.question: Are access-management operations an explicit exception to invariant 2, or must the acting administrator also have a grant or assignment for the project?
options: Access-management operations are exempt from the project grant/assignment requirement
Administrators need a project grant or assignment as well as access-management capability
open_points.default_guess: Treat access-management operations as an explicit exception.

witness.initial: An active project has no grants or assignments, and an administrator has an active session and access-management capability.
events: The administrator attempts to create the project's first staff assignment.
outcomes: Creation succeeds because the special access-management rule requires no pre-existing assignment.
Creation is denied because invariant 2 requires a project grant or assignment for every project-scoped access.

open_points.subject: Producer bearer transport
open_points.text: “Concrete transport between PresuPro and the portal — decided by R0-09: a bearer header only.”
open_points.question: What exact header and transport-security boundary are mandatory for producer credentials, including whether plaintext HTTP is refused and where TLS may terminate?
options: Standard Authorization: Bearer over HTTPS only, with a defined trusted TLS termination boundary
Any configured header carrying a bearer value is acceptable
Bearer authentication may be accepted over plaintext HTTP on a trusted network
open_points.default_guess: Require Authorization: Bearer over HTTPS, allowing only an explicitly trusted TLS terminator.

witness.initial: The portal is configured with an allowed host, and a producer has a valid credential.
events: The producer sends the credential in a bearer-style header over plaintext HTTP.
outcomes: The portal rejects the request because the credential transport is not confidential.
The portal accepts the request because only the header placement and trusted host were specified.
witness.observer: The producer and the network operator

open_points.subject: Producer project scope
open_points.text: A ServicePrincipal may have “allowed projects or administrative area” and “a global producer ... through an explicitly granted capability,” while invariant 2 requires a “project grant/assignment” and R0-24 describes producer grants per project.
open_points.question: Can an administrative-area or global producer scope substitute for a project-specific producer grant, and what named capability or stored grant represents that scope?
options: Every import requires a project-specific producer grant
Area scope authorizes every project in that area without individual grants
A named global-producer capability authorizes every project without individual grants
open_points.default_guess: Require a project-specific producer grant until area and global scope records and capabilities are explicitly named.

witness.initial: A producer is active, has the import capability and a stated administrative-area scope, but has no producer grant for project P.
events: The producer submits a valid snapshot for active project P inside that area.
outcomes: The import succeeds because area scope is an alternative to allowed-project grants.
The import is denied because invariant 2 and R0-24 require a project-specific producer grant.

open_points.subject: Viewer access-link issuance
open_points.text: A ViewerAccessCredential is “issued and re-issuable by an administrator” and stored only in verification form, but no text says how its one usable plaintext link reaches the administrator or viewer.
open_points.question: What does successful issue or re-issue return, to whom is the plaintext capability disclosed, and is it ever delivered by another product action?
options: Return the complete link once in the administrator's response
Deliver the link through a named external channel without returning it
Return only metadata and require a separately defined reveal action
open_points.default_guess: Return the complete link once to the authorized administrator and never make it retrievable afterward.

witness.initial: An administrator creates a viewer whose credential secret will be stored only in verification form.
events: The portal successfully issues the viewer access credential.
The administrator tries to give the viewer a usable link.
outcomes: The issue response contains the one-time plaintext link, so it can be handed over.
The response contains only credential metadata, leaving no specified actor or action able to obtain the link.

open_points.subject: Re-issuable access-management entities
open_points.text: R0-14 says “Creating, revoking and re-issuing client viewers, their access links and project grants,” although ClientViewer is described as a permanent identity and only its access credential is described as re-issuable.
open_points.question: Which entities actually support re-issue: only access links, or viewer identities and project grants too, and what does re-issue preserve or replace?
options: Only an access link can be re-issued; viewer identity and grants remain unchanged
Re-issuing a viewer creates a replacement viewer identity
Re-issuing a grant creates a replacement grant record
open_points.default_guess: Apply re-issue only to the viewer access link while preserving the permanent viewer and its grants.

witness.initial: Viewer V has grant G and access link L.
events: An administrator requests the R0-14 re-issue operation for V.
outcomes: Only L is replaced; V and G retain their identities.
V or G is replaced because R0-14 applies re-issue to all three nouns.

open_points.subject: Service-credential rotation overlap
open_points.text: Service credentials are “rotatable with an overlap period,” but the start, end, duration, configurability and effect of another rotation or revocation during that period are unnamed.
open_points.question: When rotation occurs, exactly how long does the previous credential remain valid, what stored fact ends that validity, and can an administrator terminate the overlap early?
options: A fixed product-defined overlap expires automatically
A deployment-configured overlap expires automatically
The administrator chooses an expiry for each rotation
The old credential remains valid until explicitly revoked
open_points.default_guess: Use a deployment-configured expiry recorded on the previous credential and permit explicit early revocation.

witness.initial: Producer P authenticates with credential C1.
events: An administrator rotates C1 and receives C2.
P continues using C1 after rotation.
outcomes: C1 remains valid until a defined overlap deadline.
C1 is immediately invalid, or remains valid indefinitely, because no overlap rule is concrete.

open_points.subject: Initial staff password change
open_points.text: R0-19 says “the holder logs in with the initial password and changes it” but does not say whether changing it is mandatory before other operations or merely expected procedure.
open_points.question: After first login with the administrator-chosen password, may the holder use normal capabilities before changing it, and what stored state enforces any first-login restriction?
options: All normal operations are blocked until the password is changed
The account is fully usable and changing the initial password is advisory
Only selected sensitive operations are blocked
open_points.default_guess: Require a password change before normal authenticated operations and store a must-change-password state.

witness.initial: An administrator activates a new operator account with an initial password and an assignment to active project P.
events: The holder logs in with the initial password.
Before changing it, the holder submits an expense correction for P.
outcomes: The correction is refused until the password is changed.
The correction succeeds because activation made the account fully active.

open_points.subject: First-administrator command contract
open_points.text: R0-07 says the email and password are inputs “read neither from process arguments nor from the environment nor from a file” and promises “a closed set of exit codes,” but names neither the remaining input channel nor the exit-code meanings.
open_points.question: How does the host operator supply both inputs, and what complete success and failure exit-code set may deployment scripts rely on?
options: Interactive terminal prompts with named exit codes
Standard input with a defined framing and named exit codes
An operating-system credential channel with named exit codes
open_points.default_guess: Use non-echoing interactive terminal prompts and define separate codes for success, non-empty deployment, invalid input, configuration failure and persistence failure.

witness.initial: A valid empty deployment must be bootstrapped by an automated deployment process.
events: The process invokes the local command without arguments, environment secrets or an input file.
outcomes: The command reads a documented stdin protocol and returns a documented branchable code.
The command requires an interactive terminal or uses different exit codes, so the automation cannot know how to supply inputs or classify failure.
witness.observer: The host operator and deployment script

open_points.subject: Bootstrap audit provenance
open_points.text: R0-07 says creation of the first administrator is “never ... audited,” while invariant 12 says “Every significant action carries actor provenance to audit” and staff-account creation is an access-management action.
open_points.question: Is bootstrap administrator creation an explicit exception to the audit invariant, or must an audit record identify the host/bootstrap actor without recording secrets?
options: Bootstrap is explicitly exempt from product audit
Bootstrap creates an audit record with non-secret host provenance
open_points.default_guess: Record a non-secret bootstrap audit event with host provenance.

witness.initial: The deployment contains no staff accounts.
events: A host operator successfully runs the bootstrap command and creates the first administrator.
An auditor inspects the portal audit history.
outcomes: No creation event exists, as R0-07 requires.
A staff-account creation event exists, as invariant 12 requires.

open_points.subject: Liveness and readiness semantics
open_points.text: R0-11 promises “an unauthenticated liveness and readiness check” but does not name what each check tests or the success and failure status/body.
open_points.question: What conditions make liveness and readiness succeed or fail, and what exact non-disclosing observable response distinguishes those states?
options: Liveness tests only the running process; readiness additionally tests required database and binary-root access
Both checks test only whether the HTTP process answers
Both checks include all external dependencies
open_points.default_guess: Make liveness process-only and readiness depend on required local persistence, with fixed minimal bodies and distinct success/failure HTTP statuses.

witness.initial: The HTTP process is running but its SQLite database cannot be opened.
events: An orchestrator calls liveness.
The orchestrator calls readiness.
outcomes: Liveness succeeds and readiness fails.
Both checks succeed, or both fail, because their meanings were not specified.

open_points.subject: Protected-binary concealed failure
open_points.text: R0-12 says an “unknown, cross-project, hidden, oversize or unlisted read is answered the same way” but never defines that common HTTP status, body, headers, or whether a missing external file and storage-read failure join the same class.
open_points.question: What exact response represents every concealed binary-read failure, and which storage failures are included?
options: A fixed not-found response for every listed case and missing stored bytes
A fixed forbidden response for every listed case
A generic binary-unavailable response also covering transient storage failures
open_points.default_guess: Use one fixed not-found response for authorization, visibility, identity, media-type, size and missing-byte failures, while treating transient infrastructure failure separately.

witness.initial: A viewer can read project P and requests two document IDs: one belongs to another project and one is authorized but its referenced file is missing.
events: The viewer downloads the cross-project document.
The viewer downloads the record whose bytes are missing.
outcomes: Both requests have the same fixed concealed response.
The cross-project request is concealed but missing bytes produce a distinguishable storage or server error.

open_points.subject: Deferred challenge operation responses
open_points.text: R0-15 and R0-23 say the password-reset request “answers as usual” and other deferred challenge operations answer with “the concealed authentication rejection,” but neither observable response is defined.
open_points.question: What exact status and response body does each inert challenge operation return, and does the reset-request response remain identical for existing and absent accounts and under rate limiting?
options: A fixed accepted/reset-request response and a fixed concealed-rejection response
A generic success response for every inert operation
Operation-specific concealed responses
open_points.default_guess: Define one fixed reset-request acknowledgment independent of account existence and one fixed concealed rejection for the other inert operations.

witness.initial: One submitted email belongs to an account and another does not; challenge infrastructure is deferred.
events: An unauthenticated caller requests a password reset for each email.
The caller attempts password-reset completion with an arbitrary token.
outcomes: All responses follow explicitly fixed, indistinguishable contracts.
Implementers choose different statuses or bodies for “as usual” and “concealed,” potentially exposing account existence or breaking clients.

open_points.subject: Snapshot import attempt classification boundary
open_points.text: R0-25 records “every import attempt it classifies” and excludes only failed bearer authentication, without defining which authenticated parsing, contract-validation, authorization, Registry and infrastructure failures count as classified rejections.
open_points.question: After successful bearer authentication, which failure stages must produce a fresh immutable import result and which instead return an unrecorded transport or service error?
options: Every authenticated request that can be associated with a producer gets an import result, including malformed or unauthorized input
Only syntactically valid snapshot commands get import results
Only domain validation outcomes get import results; Registry and infrastructure failures do not
open_points.default_guess: Create results for syntactically valid authenticated commands and domain or authorization rejections, but not for unreadable JSON or failures before a durable classification can be made.

witness.initial: A producer has a valid bearer credential but submits JSON lacking project_id.
events: The portal authenticates the bearer and attempts to process the body.
outcomes: A fresh rejection import result and import_id are recorded and returned.
The request receives an ordinary validation error and no import result because it was never classified as an import attempt.

open_points.subject: Identical snapshot content
open_points.text: R0-25 says “re-publishes the same snapshot: identical content” and the import rules mention a content fingerprint, but no text defines which fields and canonical representations participate in equality.
open_points.question: Do volatile provenance fields such as published_at participate in identity-content comparison, and how are object ordering, section ordering and decimal representations canonicalized before fingerprinting?
options: Fingerprint every submitted field exactly after a defined canonical JSON encoding
Fingerprint only immutable business content and exclude publication-attempt metadata such as published_at
Compare normalized domain values field by field without defining a JSON-byte canonical form
open_points.default_guess: Compare normalized immutable business fields, preserve section order where semantically relevant, and exclude publication-attempt metadata from the equality fingerprint.

witness.initial: Snapshot E version 1 was accepted with published_at T1.
events: After losing the response, the same producer republishes identical business data with published_at T2.
outcomes: The request is an idempotent replay because published_at is attempt provenance.
The request is an integrity conflict because published_at participates in the fingerprint.

open_points.subject: Authorization to read an import result
open_points.text: R0-21 says an import result is returned “only to the principal that made the import,” while invariant 2 requires current project access, capability and Registry lifecycle policy; the text never says whether an import result is itself project-scoped or whether current producer grants are rechecked.
open_points.question: Besides being the originating principal, must the caller still have an active credential, read-import-result capability, current project grant or scope, and a Registry-readable project, and what happens after grant revocation or archival?
options: Originating principal plus active authentication and capability is sufficient
Originating principal must also retain current project scope or grant and pass Registry lifecycle checks
Ownership at import time permanently authorizes result reads while the principal remains active
open_points.default_guess: Require active authentication, active principal, read-import-result capability and current project scope; allow archived-project reads but deny after grant revocation.

witness.initial: Producer P imported snapshot S for project A and received import_id I; its producer grant for A is later revoked.
events: P authenticates with another still-valid credential and requests I.
outcomes: The result is returned because P is the principal that created it.
The request is concealed as not found because P no longer has project access.

open_points.subject: Archived producer grant read access
open_points.text: R0-24 says an existing “producer grant ... keeps giving read access” after archival, but ServicePrincipal capabilities include only snapshot import and reading its own import results, and archived projects refuse snapshot import.
open_points.question: What concrete project information may a producer with an existing grant read after archival: only its own import results, snapshot records, or nothing beyond non-project result metadata?
options: Only import results created by that same principal
Imported snapshot records as well as own import results
No producer read survives archival because no general project-read capability exists
open_points.default_guess: Limit the surviving read to that principal's own import results.

witness.initial: Producer P has a grant for project A, has imported a snapshot, and A is then archived.
events: P requests its old import result.
P attempts to read the imported snapshot itself.
outcomes: Only the import-result request succeeds.
Both succeed as archived project reads, or neither succeeds because the producer has no archived-read capability.
